## TL;DR

Completed the missing headless viewport verification after review and found an Agents first-load failure bug. A failed config request previously left the page on its skeleton indefinitely. Agents now shows an accessible, actionable error card with Retry; the page hides raw initial config errors from its subtitle. Headless Playwright checked empty, loading, and error states for all three pages at 375, 768, and 1280 px: 27 captures, all expected state elements visible, no horizontal overflow, and no uncaught page errors.

## Work and rationale

The review correctly noted that the previous pass lacked viewport evidence. I resumed the active task branch and used its managed task preview with headless Playwright. For each page and width, a new browser page used a controlled route fixture to seed an empty result, hold the primary loading request open, or return a 503 for the primary data request. This isolates the intended UI state and avoids relying on mutable live data. I captured a viewport screenshot for each combination and checked the expected state selector, page errors, and document/body scroll width.

Agents used its existing `agents:empty` fixture, a pending `/api/config` route for loading, and a 503 `/api/config` route for failure. That last case revealed a genuine defect: the config store sets an error when its request fails but keeps `loaded` false, while Agents showed the skeleton whenever `loaded` was false. The error could sit unnoticed in the subtitle beneath the skeleton, leaving no retry path. I added an initial-load error card with `role="alert"`, plain-language connection guidance, and a Retry action calling `config.load()`. The skeleton now appears only when loading without an error. The subtitle reserves its raw error display for loaded configuration, so transient server details do not leak into the main page summary. A responsive card style wraps its button on narrow screens. The focused Agents test confirms alert semantics, retry copy, skeleton removal, and suppression of the raw error string.

Checks used an empty plan with `source: "empty"` and no steps, a pending `/api/check-plan`, and a 503 response. The empty plan showed the dedicated “No checks configured” reminder, not just the separate no-run message. Its longer content remains scrollable on mobile. Loading and error branches appeared at every requested width. Releases used a disabled release status for empty guidance, a pending `/api/release`, and a 503 response. Its setup guidance, loading skeleton, and alert all rendered at each width.

All 27 Playwright captures had their expected state selectors visible. Measured document and body widths did not exceed each configured viewport, and there were no uncaught page errors. I visually inspected representative mobile captures, including the Agents retry card, Checks empty-plan reminder, and Releases skeleton. Screenshot files and the JSON result summary remain in the ignored `.repoos/qa-evidence/1216/` directory. The QA report now contains the test matrix and evidence details.

## Approaches tried

The initial viewport run revealed that the already-running task preview still served the previous build, so the new Agents error UI was absent. I rebuilt the UI and restarted the managed preview before treating any captures as final. The first Checks empty response used a declared empty plan, which intentionally does not trigger the special reminder; I corrected the fixture to the domain's genuine empty-plan source and asserted the reminder itself. One mobile Agents error capture initially raced the response; the final matrix waits for each expected state selector before taking the screenshot.

I ran the focused Agents UI test after the change and rebuilt the UI for preview. The required `REPOOS_CHECK_CHANGED=main repoos check` passed after formatting. The remote run built the tree and passed all 284 scoped tests; local format, lint, build, CSS, contrast, and UI smoke checks passed.

## Challenges and blockers

The worktree instructions prohibit launching `repoos serve`, so browser verification used `repoos preview 1216`, which provides the server-owned preview. Loading fixtures deliberately left their requests pending until the screenshot was captured and page closed. Error fixtures were deterministic 503 route responses; they do not claim a live network outage. The exact requested viewport widths were all tested, and no visual overflow issue remains from these captures.

## Key learnings

A store may have an error while still reporting `loaded: false`; a view that keys only its skeleton to `!loaded` can conceal the failure forever. Loading indicators should account for the error state, and the error needs a direct recovery action. For this project, empty Checks plans also have a meaningful distinction between an empty valid plan and an empty invalid declared plan; fixtures must preserve that domain distinction to exercise the intended message. Finally, a browser viewport assertion is stronger when it checks both expected state visibility and actual document width, not only whether navigation completed.
